solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poet program occupies most of exhibit

indicators.note: the program takes up room inside the exhibit

parts.note: SHOW = exhibit, minus its final W
an app is a computer program

explanation.surface: A poet's software sits in a gallery display, taking up nearly all of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Program is the modern software sense, an unexpected neighbour for a poet from the sixth century BC.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappho is one of the most famous poets of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Buffeted small railway wagon

parts.note: s = small, as on clothing labels
in Britain an open railway goods wagon is a truck

explanation.surface: A little railway wagon is knocked about by the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: Buffeted reads as an adjective describing the wagon, but it is the past tense of a verb: hit, struck.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: waves or wind that buffet a thing hit it hard.

clue.text: Legal cases succeeded against local press agent

parts.note: your local is your nearest pub
licit = lawful
s = succeeded, the genealogy abbreviation

explanation.surface: Lawsuits are won against a regional newspaper's PR person.
explanation.walkthrough: Legal cases looks like a noun phrase about lawsuits; it is LICIT casing S. 'Local' as a noun is British for the neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A publicist handles press and publicity for a client.

clue.text: It's perfect on top of yoghurt!

definitions.text: It's perfect on top of yoghurt!

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: to hone something is to perfect or sharpen it

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of yoghurt

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic food tip: drizzling something over yoghurt makes it just right.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' puts HONE above Y, the 'top of' yoghurt. The whole clue also describes the answer, a classic topping for yoghurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey is the sweet syrup made by bees, commonly drizzled over a bowl of yoghurt.

clue.text: Dish made with eggs — some sell better without any shells

indicators.note: each word loses its outer letters, as an egg loses its shell

parts.note: sOMe without its first and last letters
sELl without its outer letters
bETTEr without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A market trader's tip: eggs sell better once you have taken the shells off.
explanation.walkthrough: The shells are the first and last letters of each of the three words; the egg imagery makes the instruction apt.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is beaten eggs cooked in a pan.

clue.text: Doctor claimed refurbished workspace next to river

indicators.note: next to sets the river letter directly after the workspace
refurbished means done up anew, so the letters of claimed are rearranged

parts.note: an office is a workspace
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of having done up their workplace beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is the definition here, not an instruction to rearrange letters; 'refurbished' does that job, and 'next to' adds the river at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical officer is a physician in charge of health in an organisation or the forces.

clue.text: Call in large loan agreements, causing reputational damage

parts.note: l = large, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: 'in' places one thing inside another, so the call sits within the loan agreements

parts.note: IOUs are written promises to repay
to bell someone is British slang for phoning them

explanation.surface: A bank calls in big loans, and its good name suffers for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Call in reads as the banking phrase for demanding repayment; here Call is BELL and in tells you where it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something libellous damages a person's reputation in writing.

clue.text: Every now and again swim past rocky peak in trunks

indicators.note: past means beyond, so the swim letters come after the peak

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or outcrop, as on Dartmoor

indicators.note: every now and again picks alternate letters of swim

parts.note: the word whose alternate letters S and I are taken

explanation.surface: Someone in swimming trunks occasionally swims beyond a craggy summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every now and again' takes S and I from swim; 'past' puts them after TOR. 'Trunks' means bodies without limbs, not swimwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Torsos, formally torsi, are human trunks: the body without head or limbs.

clue.text: Invigorate Frenchman upset with non-uniform appearance

indicators.note: with joins the two halves, the second set directly after the first
in a down clue, upset turns the name upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: Rene is a typical French man's name

indicators.note: non says the uniform letter is absent

parts.note: a guise is an outward appearance
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An instruction to liven up a disgruntled Frenchman whose looks are inconsistent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses RENE to ENER; 'non-uniform' drops U from GUISE to leave GISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise someone is to give them vigour and enthusiasm, the same as invigorating them.

clue.text: Note lines accompanying lengthy word for part of the brain

definitions.note: strictly a function of the brain rather than a physical part of it

parts.note: long = lengthy
a term is a word
a memo is a note
RY = railway, whose lines are its tracks

explanation.surface: A long technical word noted down as a label for a brain region.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines for RY is a standard crossword shorthand: railway lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-term memory is the brain's store of lasting memories.

clue.text: Heroic tale of Ohio-born Liberal Democrat

indicators.note: liberal means free and loose, so the letters of Ohio-born are treated freely

explanation.surface: A political profile: an American Liberal Democrat born in Ohio is the stuff of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like the party label but rearranges OHIOBORN into ROBINHOO; D for Democrat finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The outlaw of Sherwood Forest is the hero of a long-running English legend, so his name stands for the story.

clue.text: Seize westbound drug boat

indicators.note: in an across clue westbound means right to left, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to grab is to seize
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Police grab drugs from a vessel heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'westbound' means reading right to left. E for ecstasy is a standard crossword drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A barge is a long flat-bottomed boat used on canals and rivers.

clue.text: Life force found within Pinocchio

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the name

parts.note: the letters sit in the middle of the puppet's name, after PINO

explanation.surface: The spark that makes a wooden puppet come alive.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinocchio is the puppet who came to life, so the life force fits the story too.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi (qi) is the vital energy of Chinese philosophy.

clue.text: Compare story-telling with cartoon bear leading and jumping cross-legged

indicators.note: 'with' means together with, so the compare and story-telling pieces are joined side by side
whoever is leading walks in front, so the bear goes at the start of the answer

parts.note: Yogi Bear of the Hanna-Barbera cartoons
cf. is the abbreviation for compare
telling stories = telling lies

explanation.surface: A children's storyteller compares tales with a cartoon bear who hops about in a lotus pose.
explanation.walkthrough: Story-telling is the childish euphemism for fibbing. Yogic flying is the Transcendental Meditation practice of hopping while seated cross-legged.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogic flying is hopping along while sitting in the lotus position.

clue.text: Combine core part of chimney and old fireplace

indicators.note: the core of anything is its centre, so take the letter at the very middle of the word

parts.note: M is the central letter of chiMney
an ingle is an old word for a hearth, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: Building instructions: join the middle of the chimney stack to an antique hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: Combine is a verb here, matching mingle.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to mix things together.

clue.text: Laid songs out in series of notes

indicators.note: out means not in order, so the letters of laid songs are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lays out songs in a sequence of musical notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of LAID SONGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissando is a rapid slide through successive pitches on an instrument or voice.

clue.text: Hunter — one regularly taking fewer traps

parts.note: less = fewer
I = one, the Roman numeral
on a medicine is regularly taking it

explanation.surface: A hunter who sets fewer traps than before.
explanation.walkthrough: Regularly taking looks like an alternate-letters instruction, but it means ON, as in on statins. It is the lioness, not the lion, who does most of a pride's hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionesses do most of the hunting for a pride.

clue.text: Something that reveals palpebral muscle?

definitions.meaning: a surprising discovery that shows you something you had not seen
palpebral means of the eyelid; the muscle literally opens the eye

explanation.surface: An anatomy question about what shows the eyelid muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: Palpebral is an obscure word for 'of the eyelid'; the muscle that lifts the lid is literally an eye opener.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is a surprising revelation, and a muscle that raises the eyelid opens the eye.

clue.text: Lift across the pond to reveal rocks

indicators.note: the letters are rocked into a new order

parts.note: anagram of TO REVEAL

explanation.surface: An American lift opens to show a pile of stones.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocks is a noun in the surface but a verb here. Across the pond means in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: what Britons call a lift, Americans (across the Atlantic) call by this name.

clue.text: Set fire to gas when there's no energy left for element

parts.note: lit = set fire to

parts.words: gas when there's no energy left
parts.note: HELIUM, a gas, without E and L

explanation.surface: A chemist ignites a gas once its energy has run out, to obtain an element.
explanation.walkthrough: No energy left sounds like exhaustion; it removes two letters, E for energy and L for left.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithium is a chemical element, the lightest metal.

clue.text: Someone going through penance more quickly

definitions.meaning: one who fasts, as in Lent

explanation.surface: A penitent hurrying through their penance.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced the same but come from different roots: going without food, and speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A faster abstains from food as penance; faster also means more quickly.

clue.text: Pretence regularly cloaked by quiet delivery

indicators.note: cloaked by says the pretence letters are wrapped inside the quiet letters

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of pretence

parts.note: the word whose odd letters P, E, E, C are taken

explanation.surface: A sham, quietly concealed, is handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' means a way of speaking, not a parcel arriving; 'regularly' takes every other letter, and 'cloaked by' puts them inside the quiet letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker's delivery is their manner of speaking, so speech here means oral delivery.

clue.text: Five nudes jumping over tree backwards — it's a work of art

parts.note: V = five in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the letters of NUDES leap about

parts.note: anagram of NUDES
o = over, a cricket abbreviation
the lime or linden tree

explanation.surface: Five naked figures leap backwards over a tree, which sounds like a sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: O and LIME make OLIME, which reverses to EMILO. The nudes fit the famous armless statue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venus de Milo is the ancient Greek marble statue in the Louvre.

clue.text: Group performing without safety device?

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside

parts.note: a safety net
on = on stage, performing

explanation.surface: Trapeze artists perform without a safety net.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface splits the answer as 'no net', which is exactly the trap: 'without' here is the old sense of outside, as in the hymn line 'a green hill far away, without a city wall'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this is a group of nine performers, or a piece written for them.

clue.text: Bad egg turning green

parts.note: evil = bad
an egg is O-shaped

explanation.surface: A rotten egg going green.
explanation.walkthrough: Bad egg is a set phrase for a rogue, which hides the split between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a dull yellowish-green colour.

clue.text: Love intervening for and on behalf of father

parts.note: pp = per procurationem, written when signing for someone else
love = zero in tennis

explanation.surface: Love steps in to speak up for Dad.
explanation.walkthrough: pp is what you write before signing a letter on someone else's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal, chiefly American word for a dad.

clue.text: Muscle connector lacks density for part of joint

indicators.note: a thing that lacks something does not have it, so the letter for density is removed

parts.note: a tendon joins muscle to bone
d = density in physics formulas

explanation.surface: An anatomy note: a tendon missing its density, in part of a knee.
explanation.walkthrough: The anatomy surface makes you think of a body joint; the answer is a carpentry joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the projecting tongue that fits into a mortise to make a joint.

clue.text: Honour the German church incorporating new submissiveness

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take into the body of something, so 'the German church' takes the new letter into itself

parts.note: OBE = Officer of the Order of the British Empire, an honour
die = the, in German
CE = Church of England
n = new

explanation.surface: Honouring a German church that has brought in a new meekness.
explanation.walkthrough: The German looks like a nationality; it asks for the German word for 'the'. DIE and CE together take N in at their join.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name a willingness to do as one is told.

clue.text: Revised name or term accommodating latest in technology?

definitions.text: Revised name or term accommodating latest in technology?

indicators.note: accommodating means taking in, so the last letter goes inside the rearranged letters
revised means altered, so the letters are rearranged
latest in picks the final letter of technology

parts.note: the word whose last letter Y is taken

explanation.surface: Wording is updated to reflect the newest technology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revised' rearranges N plus OR TERM; 'accommodating' puts Y, the 'latest in' technology, inside. The whole clue describes such a coinage, like 'landline' after mobiles arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A retronym is a new label for an old thing, coined because newer technology made the original word ambiguous.

clue.text: Go through curved opening at 135 degrees

parts.note: on a compass, 135 degrees is south-east
an arch is a curved opening

explanation.surface: Walk through a rounded doorway set at an angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 135 degrees looks like geometry; it is a compass bearing, south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: going through someone's pockets means hunting through them.
